- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; increase forecast for next 3–5 days by 15–30% of recent peak.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and price is rising, model often over-anticipates; reduce forecast for next 3–5 days by 15–25% to avoid overshoot.
- Model consistently under-forecasts when sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward; apply a 10–20% upward bias to forecast for next 5 days.
- After a sharp spike (true outcome > 3x recent mean), model often fails to capture continuation; extend forecast horizon with 2–3 days of moderate upward slope.
- Model over-forecasts in early horizon (first 5 days) when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply 10–15% downward correction to first 5 forecast points.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of mean-reversion bias to forecast.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a spike, model often fails to adjust; apply 20–30% downward correction to next 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative.
- Model under-forecasts in high volatility periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive sentiment extremes); apply 15–25% upward bias to forecast for next 7 days.
